name: agent-builder-model-map
body:
The distributed `agent-builder` agent template `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` (product source embedded via `include_str!` and installed by `apg init` into `~/.config/opencode/agents/`) maintains the repo's `opencode.json` agent→model map, alongside scaffolding/updating `.opencode/agents/**`. `opencode.json` is a MAIN-checkout file holding per-agent `agents.<name>.model` entries under the opencode 2.x `agents` key (a reference carrying a variant joins as `provider/model#variant`); populating it rides the SAME agent-builder carve-out as `.opencode/agents/**` (see `global.constraint.worktree-isolation` and `requirements.constraint.agent-changes-always-on-main`) — one of the agent-builder's carve-out-1 write paths, under the same carve-out rather than a third carve-out.

Required behaviour:
- INTERVIEW: when scaffolding/updating agents, the agent-builder asks the coordinator/user (one question at a time; multiple-choice preferred) whether the user wants specific model mappings for the agents it scaffolds AND for the distributed suite agents, and it records the chosen `agents.<name>.model` values.
- WRITE/MERGE: it creates or updates `opencode.json` at the repo root, adding/updating ONLY the `agents.<name>.model` entries the interview produced. The write MERGES: every other key and every existing entry survives unless the interview changes it — clobbering of unrelated config is absent.
- EXCLUSION: `codebase-navigator` carries zero model mapping; the interview excludes it and the merge writes zero `agents.codebase-navigator.model` key.
- GRANT: the template's own `permissions` array carries the `edit` rule that grants the repo-root `opencode.json` ALONGSIDE `.opencode/agents/**`, so the instruction is executable and an implementer adds zero prose the agent lacks permission to carry out. The `edit` rule stays deny-by-default with EXACTLY two allow entries — `.opencode/agents/**` and `opencode.json` — resolved against the session workspace root (the main checkout) exactly like the existing `.opencode/agents/**` grant. It is zero worktree-scoped mirror (`apg/.worktrees/*/opencode.json` is excluded) and zero broader glob (`*.json`, `**`, or any other pattern).

Acceptance criteria:
- The template instructs the agent-builder to create/update the repo-root `opencode.json` alongside `.opencode/agents/**`, on the main checkout.
- The template's `permissions` array covers exactly the repo-root `opencode.json` in addition to `.opencode/agents/**`: the `edit` action deny-by-default with the only allow entries being `.opencode/agents/**` and `opencode.json`, main-checkout-resolved like the `.opencode/agents/**` grant — zero `apg/.worktrees/*/opencode.json` mirror and zero broader glob such as `*.json` or `**`.
- The template carries an interview step that asks for `agents.<name>.model` preferences for the agents it scaffolds and the distributed suite agents, and records the answers.
- A write MERGES: existing `opencode.json` entries and unrelated keys survive unless the interview changes them.
- `codebase-navigator` is explicitly excluded from model mapping.
- Scope is the one product-source file `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`; the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` and the repo's own `opencode.json` are consumer artifacts; zero binary change.
